hints.title: Duplicate Inflection Ambiguity
hints.text: When elements at left, middle, and right are identical, how can you determine which side contains the sorted sequence? What safe boundary shift preserves completeness?

hints.title: Equality Truncation Invariant
hints.text: If nums[left] == nums[mid] == nums[right], decrement right and increment left. Otherwise, at least one half is strictly sorted and can be verified.

hints.title: Conditional Halving Procedure
hints.text: Compare nums[left] and nums[mid]. If nums[left] == nums[mid] == nums[right], adjust left += 1 and right -= 1. If the left half is sorted, check if target falls in [nums[left], nums[mid]) to shrink right; otherwise search left half. Handle the symmetric right-sorted branch identically.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Logarithmic bisection on distinct segments degrading to linear only when all boundaries share identical duplicate values.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Identical values at boundaries obscure whether the inflection point lies in the left or right subsegment.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Shifting pointers in-place requires zero auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why duplicates degrade worst-case runtime to O(N) and correctly shrinking both ends when ambiguous.
